recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. Future work should only change this area if PA reopens the team or location participation model; adding redundant prose now would not improve conformance guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-35841 asked Patient Administration to align Appointment and Encounter participant.actor descriptions because Appointment wording implied a single person while Encounter wording implied multiple persons, creating confusion around teams, groups, CareTeams, and locations.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by b7582c9d7020a991a7322807df613eb376efea15, which updated the Appointment and Encounter participant.actor short/definition text and added the Encounter planning comment. Commit 0d29ecdb218f70c294183b3135c6224848fb2e44 then adjusted the wording from "may not" to "might not" without changing the model.
additional_context: FHIR-34141, the predecessor cited by the seed issue, was Resolved - No Change and confirms that an Appointment CareTeam participant is singular in nature: a specific member is selected, and multiple needed members are represented by repeating the CareTeam participant. PA January 2022 WGM minutes record the FHIR-35841 discussion and persuasive disposition. Later FHIR-32347 appended Encounter guidance about optional actors without reversing the CareTeam/Location distinction.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. Appointment and Encounter are active build resources, and the current StructureDefinition XML already has Appointment.participant.actor including CareTeam and Location planning targets plus the single-member CareTeam comment, while Encounter.participant.actor uses the aligned individual/device/service wording and excludes CareTeam and Location targets.

related_jiras.note: Predecessor no-change issue explaining why CareTeam appointment participation remains singular and does not require encounter-participant-type value set expansion.
Later Encounter participant.actor guidance added optional-actor text while preserving the FHIR-35841 wording and target-profile distinction.
